source.title: Break a Lag: Triple Exponential Moving Average for Enhanced Optimization
source.authors: Roi Peleg; Yair Smadar; Teddy Lazebnik; A. Hoogi

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive and SGD optimizers on vision tasks using task performance, but does not measure the training–test gap directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on vision benchmarks. Its FAME-versus-other-optimizers findings are not rows because FAME is the study's own new method; rows below retain reported Adam and SGD results that bear on V4. The paper does not test memorization, architecture, batch size, explicit regularization, model size, or generalization measures.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own Adam-versus-SGD held-out classification results relevant to V4. It uses comprehensive tuning beyond learning rates and schedules, so it does not directly test V4's limited-tuning condition. A training–test gap is not required to compare held-out performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that FAME improves performance, stability, robustness, and convergence across vision tasks; the conclusion reports superiority in 86.67% of evaluated models and a 23.7% reduction in average convergence time.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces FAME using triple exponential moving averages and compares it with several optimizers; conducts grid search for optimizer hyperparameters.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences by dataset, task, model, and optimizer; FAME's additional parameters are described as fixed across experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam has lower object-detection mAP than SGD on MS-COCO and Pascal-VOC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizers can yield worse held-out object-detection performance than SGD under comprehensive tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 4 reports higher Cityscapes segmentation scores for Adam than SGD in all seven models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam can outperform SGD on semantic segmentation under comprehensive tuning.

record.problems: No direct training-versus-test gap is reported. The relevant comparisons cover vision tasks only; reported table uncertainties are standard deviations across three initializations.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for FAME, the study's proposed method, whose optimizer-performance comparisons are excluded by the row rules. Other optimizer and model table entries are not retained because the V4-relevant Adam-versus-SGD comparisons are represented by the reported task rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width changes beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Limited tuning restricted to learning rates and schedules; language benchmarks; training-performance comparisons; switching optimizers; and whether expanding tuning or decoupling weight decay causes a change in the Adam–SGD ranking.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and comparing with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 contains mixed classification rankings omitted explicitly by rows_left_out: Adam exceeds momentum SGD in 10 of 15 listed CIFAR-100 configurations and three of five ImageNet configurations; SGD wins the others. Consequently, R5 cannot summarize the study's classification evidence as uniformly favoring SGD. These declared omissions receive no additional row-based verdict here. The table contains 15 CIFAR-100 entries despite the prose claiming 17. Table 4's segmentation results do not extend V4's stated task scope. Comprehensive tuning alone does not establish that broader tuning removed or reversed an earlier gap.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening beyond interpolation and test-error changes.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.

Language benchmarks; limited tuning of only learning rates and decay schedules; decoupled weight decay and switching from Adam to SGD; broader tuning effects; the specific word-level language-model exception; direct training-versus-test performance comparison.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
